message.content:
### Hydrogen – A Quick Reference to Its Key Properties

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| **Physical State at STP** | State | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (−423.2 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (−434.2 °F) |
| | Density (gas) | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (gas, 25 °C) | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Heat of fusion | 0.000 kJ mol⁻¹ (negligible) |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Electrical conductivity | 0.000 S m⁻¹ (non‑metal) |
| | Refractive index | 1.00028 (visible light) |
| | Speed of sound | 1270 m s⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (H₂) |
| | Bonding | Forms covalent bonds; H₂ is a diatomic molecule with a single σ bond |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive with many elements; forms hydrides with metals, acids with non‑metals |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (H⁺ donor) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺) |
| | Redox behavior | Can be oxidized to water (H₂O) or reduced to hydrogen gas (H₂) |
| | Combustion | Combines with O₂ → H₂O (exothermic) |
| | Photochemical behavior | UV light can dissociate H₂ into two H atoms |
| | Isotopic effects | Deuterium and tritium form heavier hydrides; kinetic isotope effects influence reaction rates |
| **Spectroscopic Features** | Rotational spectrum | Microwave region; J=1→0 transition at 1420 MHz (21 cm line) |
| | Vibrational frequency (H₂) | ~4401 cm⁻¹ |
| | Electronic transitions | UV–visible absorption in excited states (rare in ground state) |
| **Miscellaneous** | Magnetic moment | 1 µB (electron spin) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 1 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Stability | Stable as a diatomic gas under normal conditions; unstable as isolated atom |
| | Occurrence | Most abundant element in the universe; found in stars, interstellar medium, and planetary atmospheres |
| | Uses | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), feedstock (ammonia synthesis, methanol production), cryogenic coolant, laboratory standard gas |

---

#### Quick Takeaways

- **Hydrogen is the simplest element**: one proton, one electron, and no neutrons in its most common isotope (protium).
- **It exists as a diatomic gas (H₂)** under normal conditions, with a very low boiling point and density.
- **Chemically, it is versatile**: it can act as an acid, a base, a reducing agent, or a ligand in metal complexes.
- **Isotopic variants** (deuterium, tritium) are crucial in nuclear fusion research and in tracing biochemical pathways.
- **Spectroscopically, hydrogen’s 21‑cm line** is a cornerstone of radio astronomy, mapping hydrogen distribution in galaxies.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
